rationale: While seminal delineation cohorts (such as Cannaerts et al. 2019) focus on delineating thoracic aortic aneurysms in SMAD2 carriers, the available literature excerpts do not provide explicit confirmation of the 10/15 numerator/denominator within the text. Furthermore, reviews on the genetic architecture of thoracic aortic disease (Meester et al. 2022) indicate that patients harboring TGF-beta pathway variants, including SMAD2, can present with acute aortic dissection with little or no preceding aneurysm warning, complicating the hypothesis that acute dissection is exceedingly rare or secondary compared to isolated dilation at presentation.

evidence.text: The 2019 phenotypic delineation cohort evaluated five families with novel pathogenic SMAD2 variants, confirming arterial aneurysms and dissections and phenotypic overlap with SMAD3 carriers, though specific numerical carrier breakdowns are partially truncated in the provided abstract.

conflicts: Foundational discovery reports identified acute arterial dissections alongside aneurysms as an initial defining feature, challenging the assertion that acute dissection is negligible at ascertainment.

Comprehensive reviews highlight that SMAD2 syndrome carriers can experience acute aortic dissection with little to no prior aortic root enlargement, warning against relying strictly on aneurysm dilation thresholds for surveillance.

new_directions.question_text: What is the penetrance and median age of onset of acute aortic dissection versus isolated thoracic aneurysm in larger international SMAD2 registries?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether dissection occurs below traditional surgical diameter cutoffs in SMAD2 will establish whether its natural history resembles the aggressive course of SMAD3/TGFBR-related LDS.
